notes.title: Romans: Age of Caesar Launches on Mobile!
notes.notes:
[h1] Brand new MMORTS from Firefly Studios, Romans: Age of Caesar, is now available on IOS and Android! [/h1]

Firefly Studios is proud to announce that Romans: Age of Caesar, the latest and most ambitious online title from the creators of Stronghold, [b] has now launched on mobile! To celebrate this achievement,  earn 20% bonus Trajans on each purchase made before October 7th! [/b]

Romans: Age of Caesar is a new co-op MMORTS with a plethora of city-building mechanics and features, crowned by an expansive political endgame. With development guided by several members of the original Caesar team across various disciplines, we’ve been striving to recapture the essence of that historic setting in the MMO genre.

Who better to discuss exactly what makes this new historical MMORTS special than Mr Firefly himself, Simon Bradbury, the veteran designer and coder for the Stronghold and Caesar series: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jCA81WbtsiM

Our goal with Romans has always been to give players the opportunity to experience first-hand the depth of structural planning, martial prowess and political strategy necessary to build, sustain and expand a functioning Roman city and economy, complete with other real-time players to aid or hinder you in your journey.

With multiple shared worlds and a full co-op experience on offer, lead the greatest warriors of the ancient world against the barbarian hordes or test your mettle against worthy foes in PvP by claiming victory through strategic warfare and political subterfuge. Whether through cunning or confrontation, combine your strengths with others for the good of your cities and for the glory of the empire. To have any hope of succeeding, you must be willing to do everything it takes to achieve ultimate power and be crowned Caesar.

On the go via [url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.fireflystudios.romans&hl=en_IN]Android [/url] and [url=https://apps.apple.com/au/app/romans-age-of-caesar/id1620571732]IOS[/url] on mobile or at home on PC through Steam, the restoration of Rome waits for no one! [u] Join the ranks of thousands of Governors already online in Romans: Age of Caesar to rebuild Rome together! [/u]

notes.title: Version 1.8.0
notes.notes:
--[b]Additions[/b]--
PLAYER SUGGESTED - The Dux of Houses are now able to select a House Mail option in the communications area to send mails to all members of their House and/or all Princeps of Alliances within their House for better communication

--[b]Changes[/b]--
- Imperial Points raids now steal a fixed % of a targets Imperial Points, rather than a possible range (but remains capped by your personal Imperial Points Cap
- Imperial Points Raid research now improves the fixed % you can raid from a target, starting at 50% and increasing up to 100%
PLAYER SUGGESTED - Votes for Praefectus' now decay at variable rates based on player activity. If a Praefectus disappears for multiple days, their votes will rapidly decay allowing a City to more easily elect a new Leader
PLAYER SUGGESTED - All players are now removed from the Antechamber at the end of an Epoch (meaning players are entirely removed from the Senate at the close of each Epoch)
- Legions are now required to be present as a Defender on a location in order to 'top it up' with Imperial Points for defense
- Removed the option to Auto-Resolve a PvP battle. This was proving to offer an unnecessary advantage to PvP battles since adding concurrent PvP battles and needed to be removed without impacting PvE experiences
- Senate Attacks no longer have a random element and instead have a deterministic outcome based on your Power and the Power of your Target. During a Senate Attack, The Attackers power is removed from the Defender and the Defenders Power is removed from the Attacker.
PLAYER SUGGESTED - Reduced the cost of all Senate Seats in the Conclave by roughly 40%
PLAYER SUGGESTED - Reduced the incrementor costs of all Senate Seats in the Conclave by roughly 40%
- General improvements to Wall placements in Fort Designing (this is part of ongoing improvements to Fort Designing) 

--[b]Fixes[/b]--
PLAYER REPORTED - Resolved an issue causing player Seals to display the default seal while in The Senate
PLAYER REPORTED - Fixed an issue that could allow some players to continue receiving the Imperial Points benefit of a Senate Seat they no longer held
PLAYER REPORTED - Improved the rate at which Glory Round winners are calculated
PLAYER REPORTED - Improved the system surrounding Stronghold states when ownership rapidly changes and added additional monitoring to keep and eye on the system

Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears! Today we proudly announce that [b]Romans: Age of Caesar[/b] is out now and free to play on Steam!

A brand new co-op city builder from a team of veteran Caesar developers, [b]Romans: Age of Caesar[/b] is the latest historical strategy game from our team here at Firefly Studios. Players must rebuild the once great empire as they share resources, re-establish trade routes and protect their cities from barbarian invasion. Experience classic city builder gameplay across a sprawling online empire as you build, trade and fight alongside fellow players in a shared open world. Revive the republic and restore the Roman Empire to its former glory!

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/7c160cbc2574b954ca96853616ac1dbf5f038299.png[/img]

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-5lU75Kc_F4]In our last Romans video[/url] we discussed what made the empire such a compelling setting for videogames and entertainment in the centuries following its collapse. To further discuss exactly what makes this setting and our new historical MMORTS special, we have none other than Firefly Studios co-founder Simon Bradbury, creator of Stronghold and former designer on the Caesar series!

Assembling each ancient city state from its early foundations into a flourishing beacon of civilization will be a puzzle to solve. From its architectural layout and strategic defences to your economic establishments and cultural backbone, it takes serious effort to rebuild Rome... Which is why you’ll be doing it alongside 15 other Governors! Pool responsibilities and resources to advance your shared city and then expand your influence over thousands of other players across the empire.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/9644838b169e9c7cc19ddb4b7fbb5b0bf0301d37.png[/img]

This cooperative gameplay extends to the wider region, with countless other player cities led by their own ruling Governors. This can take the form of negotiating trading routes, exchanging supplies, developing new goods, combating barbarian hordes and extending the frontiers. Eventually with a network of cities established you will form a new Roman Empire, a commonwealth of a size and scope the world has never witnessed!

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/ccf53a8d9008713b74f9ae239e7e8672a7413d63.png[/img]

Within this network of factions vying for supremacy there is the grand Roman Senate, a political endgame that will decimate all but the most shrewd power brokers. The road will be long, but the rewards are more than plentiful for those deemed worthy of them. Be crowned as Caesar himself and have your name echoed throughout the ages.

notes.title: Romans: Age of Caesar - Coming April 27th 2022!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-5lU75Kc_F4
As we approach the Steam launch of our upcoming online co-op city builder [b]Romans: Age of Caesar[/b] on April 27th, we wanted to discuss ancient Rome and its collective hold on us as developers. Through its influence across law, architecture, trade, military tactics, art and craftsmanship, Rome well and truly has its hold on us here at Firefly as we approach release.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/f980581db0cacb68b9c24cd784fb12e97a537058.jpg[/img]

Today we're incredibly excited to talk about why the Eternal City and the empire that blossomed from its industrious seed came to be the setting for our latest and most ambitious online game yet. Gaming is unique in its capacity to allows players to actively engage with historical settings, making your experience far more personal as a result of being active participants, instead of just passive observers. With [b]Romans: Age of Caesar[/b] we can't wait to see how players' political ambitions, city builder expertise and tactical military might plays out across our constantly growing empire map.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/96e384cf55d53f533819a7e5cfbc14bc815c3a8e.jpg[/img]

While every genre chooses different dimensions of this great civilization to examine, in Romans we’re particularly interested in bringing to life architectural, economic and political planning needed to transform a city on the southern Italian peninsula into an continent-spanning empire that lasted for centuries through natural disasters, civil wars, barbarian invasions and power-hungry tyrants.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/821a228aedcf1a53d67fac90ba1bf9c4c173ef15.jpg[/img]

So join us as we examine the many advances in our ability to recreate ancient Rome, in everything from music and design to visual art and gameplay. Then prepare for our latest release, which promises to build upon the classic city-building heritage that Firefly Studios is known for in an entirely new online world.

Stay tuned for more upcoming information about Romans, the Stronghold series and future of Firefly Studios. For now we can’t wait for you to get your hands on [b]Romans: Age of Caesar[/b] for free on Steam on April 27th!

notes.title: MMO city builder Romans: Age of Caesar launches this month
notes.notes:
They say Rome wasn't built in a day, and it certainly wasn't built by one person. Romans: Age of Caesar is a city-building game in the works at Firefly Studios, the developers of the Stronghold series. The Romans: Age of Caesar release date is set for April 27, Firefly has announced.

Romans: Age of Caesar is what Firefly Studios describes as an 'MMORTS.' It draws from the experience of the original design team that worked on the Impressions classic Caesar III, giving players the chance to build and administer a classical-era Roman city. The new wrinkle in Romans: Age of Caesar is that you're building your city cooperatively - up to 16 players can be working together on a single city, and those cities all form part of a Roman nation created collectively by thousands of players.

As your city grows and becomes more prosperous, you'll want to establish trade routes, which you'll need to protect from barbarian raiders. There are real-time tactical battles to fight when raids happen, or when you get into territory disputes with other players that can't be peacefully resolved.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Romans: Age of Caesar - Q&A (Part 1)
notes.notes:
Today Nick and Aaron don authentic Roman garbs to do one thing and one thing only... Answer your most pressing questions about [b]Romans: Age of Caesar[/b]! Romans is our free upcoming co-op city builder MMO, currently playable in the February Steam Next Fest.

If you caught yesterday's stream - in which Firefly Studios' Lead Designer Simon Bradbury treated us to a flood off Caesar 3-related memories - you'll know that we have a new kind of strategy MMO on the way. Today's Q&A will be the first of two parts, aiming to reveal all we can at this stage of development. So watch us deal with the biggest and most pressing questions, along with a healthy dose of playful comments and Monty Python references! Find out about Romans' graphical style, RTS elements, barbarian hordes, territory control, gameplay and more! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41187904/1f01eef89f33880f86e857a301a9d64c530be32e.jpg[/img]

As an added treat today's stream will be introduced by Firefly co-founders and Impressions Games alumni Eric Ouellette and Simon Bradbury, gracing our screens to reveal the origins and future of our recently-announced online city builder. Tracing their professional roots back to past studios and a certain roman city builder that started it all, Simon and Eric discuss how all roads have led to Romans. Having designed, produced, composed music and created art for a number of classic period city builders, many of Firefly’s current day staff and collaborators are mining their rich strategy heritage for our new MMO. Add this to Firefly’s experience developing CivCity: Rome and you have the perfect team to take this classic gameplay online in Romans: Age of Caesar.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/872570/Romans_Age_of_Caesar/

notes.title: Legacy of Romans: Age of Caesar
notes.notes:
Today we bring you a very special 'Let's Play' featuring city-building classic Caesar 3, starring Impressions Games designer and coder - and now Firefly Studios Lead Designer - Simon Bradbury!

Now that our upcoming online city builder Romans: Age of Caesar is available to download in demo form during the February Steam Next Fest, we thought we'd turn back the clocks to a time of floppy disks and CRT monitors. So join us as we explore the strategy gaming legacy of Firefly Studios and our brand new Roman empire builder!

So whether you're an old school player and devotee of the first golden age of city sim games or a developer looking for insight into the creative process as a lone freelancer and studio head - We have you covered.

notes.title: Romans: Age of Caesar - Now in Open Beta!
notes.notes:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uRNspYlaZu0

It brings us great pleasure to announce that we have just launched our open beta for [b]Romans: Age of Caesar[/b]! With Romans' first gameplay trailer also being released, its full speed ahead for our new co-op strategy MMO as we begin the march toward a full Steam launch in 2022.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/3952950/19692ebea2b057b8c2e09e65f2560519ca0f43e9.gif[/img]

From the minds of former Impressions Games developers Simon Bradbury, Eric Ouellette and Darrin Horbal comes [b]Romans: Age of Caesar[/b], the latest historical strategy game from the folks here at Firefly Studios. Romans sees city states of up to 16 players rebuilding the empire as they share resources, re-establish trade routes and protect allied cities from barbarian invasion. Classic city builder gameplay is taken online across the Roman Empire as players build, trade and fight alongside fellow would-be senators in a shared open world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/3952950/24b0afd960d312d3e77e5a9fae5103eac1ec3637.gif[/img]

Featuring 16 players per city and thousands more active across the empire, players must cooperate in order to rebuild Rome. Beyond their district lies an expansive empire map, where you can build new settlements, discover resources and team up with otherwise rival city states. Sharpen those legions and engage in tactical combat to push back barbarian frontiers in PvE or engage in political warfare, forging alliances to claim glory in epic PvP battles. Battle or build alongside fellow players, defeating common threats and building the prosperity of each shared city.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/3952950/cb43957e88338711261599235f08b142c163f1d2.gif[/img]

While the ultimate goal is to be crowned Caesar, players must first work their way up through the senate before reaching the political endgame. Earning the confidence of their political allies and either rising with them through the chambers or betraying them at the opportune moment. Manoeuvre between different loyalties, positions and gods, to remain politically nimble and succeed in the final quest for power. Dare to become emperor and have your name known across the empire.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/3952950/69b36e9f66f4950d69857ecc85e04dc8af790a05.gif[/img]

Scheduled for release on Steam in 2022, [b]Romans: Age of Caesar[/b] is now in open beta, with players able to sign up and play the game for free via the official website. Those waiting for the full Steam launch next year can also wishlist the game via the link below.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/872570/Romans_Age_of_Caesar/
